topic: Supply chain security for Python and Node.js dependencies

post.topic: Supply chain security for Python and Node.js dependencies
post.linkedin_text:
Never blindly install packages from PyPI or npm without checking.

Recent supply chain attacks on popular open-source packages prove that even trusted registries can host credential stealers and backdoors. As full-stack developers, we pull in dozens of third-party libraries daily.

Protecting your apps doesn't require paranoia, just practical safeguards:

• Pin exact dependency versions in your package.json or requirements.txt
• Use lockfiles and audit commands in your CI pipeline
• Audit maintainer changes and download counts before adding new packages
• Never run untrusted scripts or install unknown libraries on your main work machine

Security is part of the architecture, not an afterthought.

slides.title: Stop *Blindly* Installing Open-Source Packages
slides.body: Protect your Python and Node.js projects from supply chain attacks.

slides.title: Always pin exact versions
slides.body: Avoid using loose version ranges like caret or tilde in production. Pinning exact versions prevents malicious updates from sneaking into your builds.

slides.title: Automate audits in CI
slides.body: Catch known vulnerabilities and compromised packages before they reach production servers.
slides.code:
npm audit
pip-audit
# Run these on every PR

slides.title: Check package health
slides.body: Before adding a new library, look at its download stats, recent commit activity, and repository maintainers to spot anomalies.
